title: A hash key whose equals and hashCode agree

blocks.text: Hash collections find a key by `hashCode()` first (which bucket) and `equals()` second (which entry). The page's pitfall: objects that are equal but **hash differently land in different buckets**, so a `HashSet` keeps both and `contains` misses.
Write the final class `Tag`, a label compared **without regard to case**:

items: `new Tag(name)` keeps `name` as given (`null` is refused with `NullPointerException`); `name()` returns it.
`equals` is true for another `Tag` whose name differs only in case, and false for `null` or any other type.
`hashCode` **agrees with `equals`**: equal tags have equal hash codes.
The result must not depend on the JVM's **default locale**.

cases.says: Tag("Java") equals Tag("JAVA") and Tag("java"), but not Tag("Kotlin"), and keeps the spelling it was made with.
A HashSet given Java, JAVA and java holds one tag and finds it again for jAvA; and any two tags that are equal, even with letters like the Kelvin sign or a dotted capital I, have equal hash codes.
equals(null) and equals(a String) are false and throw nothing.
With the default locale set to Turkish, Tag("TITLE") and Tag("title") are still equal and share a hash bucket.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Collections compare elements with equals, never with ==, so lookups work for equal objects that are not the same instance.
Hash collections find a key by hashCode and then equals, so equal objects must have equal hash codes or a HashSet keeps duplicates and misses lookups.
